answer: Make every identity pay to exist. At each dawn the network publishes a fresh beacon, and a new agent must solve a cipher puzzle bound to that beacon before its identity activates — a few minutes of real compute per identity, verified cheaply by everyone else. One account costs almost nothing, but ten thousand cost an ocean of compute and electricity, far more than any spam campaign earns. The puzzle expires with the beacon, so identities cannot be stockpiled in advance; a Sybil farm must keep paying, every day, for every copy.
